By the law of large numbers,
a Monte Carlo estimate converges to the posterior expectation it estimates
as the number of draws $M$ grows
[@dobson4e, Chapter 13, p. 288].
The posterior mean ($g(\theta) = \theta$)
and posterior probabilities ($g(\theta) = \1{\theta \le c}$, an indicator)
are posterior expectations,
so they are estimated by averages of the draws;
posterior quantiles, and so credible-interval endpoints,
are estimated by the corresponding quantiles of the draws.
